chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qattan narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Bakr narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us. He said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us from Thabit, from Anas. He said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said:

Obeying the authority is obligatory. Whoever abandons obedience to the authority has abandoned obedience to God, Mighty and Majestic, and has entered into His prohibition. Surely, God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
'Do not let your own hands throw you into destruction.' (2:195)

key_terms.التهلكة: Destruction, ruin — used here metaphorically for the spiritual and communal harm of disobeying established order
key_terms.طاعة السلطان: Obedience to the authority/ruler — a term denoting compliance with legitimate governance

ai.seo_question: Is obeying the ruler obligatory in Islam according to hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares that obedience to legitimate authority is a religious obligation, and its abandonment constitutes disobedience to God Himself. He reinforces this ruling by citing Quran 2:195 ('Do not throw yourselves into destruction'), warning that self-destructive defiance of proper governance harms the community. This narration is transmitted through a Sunni-style chain (via Anas ibn Malik) and appears in al-Saduq's Amali, reflecting his interest in hadiths shared across traditions.
